issues.description: Interface name/type mismatch: the problem statement and template refer to a Rideable interface (with method messageOnRide()) that animals like Pig and Seal should implement, but the solution repository replaces/duplicates this with a Mountable interface which Pig and Seal implement. Additionally, Rideable.java in the solution is empty. This naming/type inconsistency between Rideable (expected) and Mountable (used) can confuse students and cause tests or examples (and the template Main.java) to fail to compile if they expect Rideable.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Replace Mountable with Rideable in the solution (or conversely, update problem/template to use Mountable). Ensure Rideable.java in the solution declares the messageOnRide() method and that Pig and Seal implement Rideable (and update their implements clauses accordingly). This preserves the intended design and avoids confusing students or breaking tests that expect Rideable.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a Rideable interface (and expect animals like Pig and Seal to implement Rideable), but the solution uses an interface named Mountable for the same concept. Additionally, the solution repository contains an effectively empty Rideable.java file while Pig and Seal implement Mountable. This inconsistent naming (Rideable vs Mountable) for the same conceptual entity (animals that can be ridden) creates a mapping barrier: students reading the problem/template will look for Rideable, but the solution code uses Mountable, causing confusion about which interface to implement and verify.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's Mountable interface to Rideable (or vice versa consistently across problem/template), and update Pig.java and Seal.java to implement Rideable. Ensure Rideable.java in the solution contains the interface definition with the method signature: public interface Rideable { String messageOnRide(); } and remove or replace any empty/duplicate Rideable.java file. This makes the conceptual entity name consistent between problem, template, and solution.
